strings.ui.journal.empty.tasks: No tasks yet. Those who listen to people are sometimes asked for something.
strings.ui.tasks.here_one: Someone here is still waiting for someone to listen.
strings.ui.tasks.here: {n} people here are still waiting for someone to listen.
strings.task.karsk.train.title: A green signal
strings.task.karsk.train.summary: An old woman and her grandchild have been waiting since yesterday for the train to Sverdlovsk. It is no longer on the board.
strings.task.karsk.train.hint.family: Talk to the old woman waiting on the platform with her grandchild.
strings.task.karsk.train.hint.signalbox: Call up to the signal box and ask what has become of the train to Sverdlovsk.
strings.task.karsk.train.hint.vendor: The driver of the mail train has his tea at the tea stall in the mornings. Talk to the tea seller.
strings.task.karsk.train.hint.return: Take the old woman the news about the mail train.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.signalbox.title: Non-stop
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.signalbox.promp: Call up to the signal box
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.signalbox.text: I call up to the signal box. Semjon slides the window open a crack, leafs through the timetable book and reads it out as if it were the weather forecast: since Monday the Sverdlovsk train has been running straight through, priority to corridor traffic; it won’t stop until the East Junction. Then, more quietly: the six-forty mail train stops there too. And Tolja, who drives it, has his tea at the tea seller’s first.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.title: Tea for Tolja
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.text: The tea seller will pass a message to the mail train’s driver. For that she even brings out the sugar.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.l1: Is Tolja driving the mail train tomorrow?
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.l2: At six he’ll be standing here like every morning, wanting tea without sugar. Like everyone.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.l3: Tell him two passengers ride in the luggage van as far as the East Junction. An old woman and a child. I’ll sign the consignment note.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.l5: For two passengers. Strangers haven’t been standing on my platform since yesterday.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.l6: Then Tolja gets a glass with sugar tomorrow. Because I do have some after all – for emergencies.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.vendor.l8: A driver in a bad mood is always an emergency, Engineer.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.title: An egg is an egg
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.text: No green signal, but two places in the mail train’s luggage van. The old woman paid with an egg, which is expressly not a bribe.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l1: Well, sonny? Have you turned a signal green for us?
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l2: No. The Sverdlovsk train doesn’t stop in Karsk any more. It runs through – corridor traffic has priority.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l3: Priority. I remember that word from forty-one.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l4: But tomorrow at six-forty the mail train runs to the East Junction, and the Sverdlovsk train still stops there. There’s room for two in the luggage van. I’ve signed the consignment note.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l5: In the luggage van. Like parcels.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l6: Like parcels someone is waiting for.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l7: You sign for an old woman you don’t know. – Here, take it. An egg isn’t a bribe, sonny. An egg is an egg.
strings.explore.karsk.task.train.return.l9: We were always on time. The trains weren’t.
strings.task.berlin.mittens.title: Knock twice
strings.task.berlin.mittens.summary: Frau Lenz’s daughter waits in the stairwell after school, because children are not allowed in the archive. Her mittens are drying on the radiator in the reading room.
strings.task.berlin.mittens.hint.take: Fetch the mittens from the radiator in the reading room.
strings.task.berlin.mittens.hint.door: Knock on the stairwell door – twice.
strings.task.berlin.mittens.hint.return: Take the porter what Lotte gave you for him.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.ask.title: A word
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.ask.text: The porter may not leave his lodge. The mittens of Frau Lenz’s little girl are drying in the reading room, and she herself is sitting outside on the stairs.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.ask.l1: Herr Adler, a word. You’ll be going through the reading room later, won’t you?
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.ask.l3: The little one’s mittens are drying on the radiator in there. Frau Lenz is taking dictation till twelve, and I’m not allowed to leave the gate. Regulations.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.ask.l4: And if you did, just this once?
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.ask.l5: Then the head of department would turn up that very minute. That’s a regulation too. It just isn’t written down anywhere.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.ask.l7: She’s sitting outside on the stairs. Knock twice, then she’ll know you’re not from the authorities.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.take.title: Lotte’s mittens
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.take.text: The mittens are warm and still damp at the thumbs. Inside, someone has embroidered a name in cross-stitch: Lotte. The librarian watches me pocket them and writes something in her lending book. I take it that I have just borrowed two mittens.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.door.title: For Mr Porter
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.door.text: I knock twice. On the third step sits a girl with a satchel, counting the tiles; she takes the mittens without looking up and holds out a folded sheet in return. On it, the porter in his lodge, the radio beside him, and musical notes flying out of the radio. “For Mr Porter. But don’t pin it up.” Children know exactly what one may pin up in a porter’s lodge.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.title: Turn it down
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.text: Lotte has her mittens. Her drawing is now in the porter’s breast pocket, next to the photo of his wife.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.l1: Lotte has her mittens. And I’m to give you this. Don’t pin it up, she said.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.l2: Well, I never. The notes are even right. That child hears better than many a block warden.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.l3: And of course you saw nothing, Herr Adler.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.l4: I saw a drawing. Of a radio.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.l5: Careful. That’s how it starts: first you see a radio, and then you hear it.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.l6: This goes in my breast pocket, with the picture of my wife. She always told me to turn it down, too.
strings.explore.berlin.task.mittens.return.l8: Nope. But she did say it.
strings.task.plaza.photo.title: A picture for the drawer
strings.task.plaza.photo.summary: The family from number nine hasn’t a single picture of their house. The albums are upstairs, behind the seal.
strings.task.plaza.photo.hint.ask: Talk to the woman from number nine again.
strings.task.plaza.photo.hint.photographer: Ask the press photographer by the chestnut stand for a picture.
strings.task.plaza.photo.hint.return: Tell the family what to watch for.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.ask.title: Not a single picture
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.ask.text: The family from number nine has no picture of their house. The albums are upstairs in the sealed flat.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.ask.l1: Sir? You look like someone who can read plans.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.ask.l3: Then you’ll know whether the house is staying.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.ask.l5: We haven’t a single picture of it. The albums are upstairs, and upstairs is sealed.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.ask.l6: The man with the camera by the chestnut stand – would he take one? Of us, in front of our door? They won’t let us leave here, after all.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.photographer.te: The photographer takes the picture from where he stands, with the long lens. If he went over, the sentry would go with him.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.photographer.l1: The family outside number nine would like a picture. Of themselves, in front of their door.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.photographer.l2: In front of a sealed door. No paper will print that, sir.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.photographer.l4: Then for the drawer. Mine is fairly full already.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.photographer.l5: I’ll take it from here, with the long lens. If I go over, the sentry comes with me.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.photographer.l6: Tell them to look over when I raise my hat. And don’t you stand with them. A man from the building office in this picture – that would be a different picture.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.title: An address
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.text: The picture is taken, from a distance and without waving. The photographer will send the print to the Building Archive, for my attention.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.l1: Look over at the chestnut stand. When the man there raises his hat: don’t wave. Just stand still.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.l2: Not wave? But you wave in photos.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.l4: Come here, Liesel. Stand up straight. Like outside church.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.l5: … He raised his hat. And where will he send the picture? We haven’t got an address.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.l6: To me. Building Archive, for the attention of Adler. I’ll bring it to you as soon as you have one.
strings.explore.plaza.task.photo.return.l7: Then at least we have an address now. Yours.
strings.task.veltrava.heating.title: Carriage three is cold
strings.task.veltrava.heating.summary: Since Kordon no heat has been reaching carriage three. Under the regulations of both sides, nobody is responsible for the heating coupling between two carriages.
strings.task.veltrava.heating.hint.ask: Talk to the conductor at carriage four.
strings.task.veltrava.heating.hint.coupling: Look at the heating coupling between carriages two and three.
strings.task.veltrava.heating.hint.kettle: Fetch hot water from the tiled stove in the waiting room.
strings.task.veltrava.heating.hint.thaw: Thaw the stopcock on the heating coupling.
strings.task.veltrava.heating.hint.return: Tell the conductor that carriage three has steam again.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.ask.title: Nobody’s responsibility
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.ask.text: Carriage three has been cold since Kordon. No annex says anything about the heating coupling between two carriages – so nobody is responsible.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.ask.l1: Engineer. Do you know anything about steam heating?
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.ask.l2: I know something about steam. About heaters that don’t heat, even more.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.ask.l3: Carriage three’s been cold since Kordon. The Moscow carriage master says the heating coupling is the train crew’s job. I’m the train crew. I’m a conductor, not a fitter.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.ask.l5: Isn’t responsible for Soviet carriages, says Annex B. Nothing anywhere about the coupling in between. And in there sit the people nobody counts: typists, the cook, two stokers.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.ask.l6: I’ll take a look at the coupling.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.coupling.t: Between carriages two and three, steam hisses into the open air: the stopcock on the heating coupling has frozen, half open, half shut. So the train is heating the platform, not the carriage. A hammer would break the plug off. Hot water won’t.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.kettle.tex: The porters by the stove look at one another when I ask for hot water. Then one of them silently fills his kettle from the stove’s water tank and wraps a rag round the handle. “For carriage three,” I say. “Nobody’s ever done anything for carriage three,” he says, first in German and then in Russian, to be sure it gets through.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.thaw.title: Steam for carriage three
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.thaw.text: I pour the water slowly over the cock until the ice cracks and the plug will turn with the square key. The hissing outside dies down; inside, the pipes begin to knock. Behind the misted window someone wipes a peephole clear and raises a hand. I raise mine too, the empty kettle in it.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.return.tex: Carriage three has steam again. The conductor brought me tea from the samovar: I am, he says, the first delegate ever to crawl under a carriage instead of into one.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.return.l1: Carriage three has steam! The typists have taken their coats off – for the first time since Kordon.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.return.l2: The stopcock was frozen. Next time hot water, not the hammer.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.return.l3: Tell that to the Moscow carriage master. No – better not tell him.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.return.l4: Here. Tea from carriage three’s samovar. It was the first thing to warm up.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.return.l6: You’re the first delegate who ever crawled under a carriage instead of into one.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.heating.return.l7: It’s more honest under a carriage. Nothing’s written on it there.
strings.task.veltrava.buffet.title: Who reaches first
strings.task.veltrava.buffet.summary: Frau Brunner has been typing since six in the morning. The buffet in the foyer is for the delegations, and nobody has helped themselves yet.
strings.task.veltrava.buffet.hint.ask: Talk to Frau Brunner in the minutes office again.
strings.task.veltrava.buffet.hint.take: Take something from the buffet in the foyer.
strings.task.veltrava.buffet.hint.journalist: Nils Ekdahl saw everything. Talk to him.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.title: Tea from twelve
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.text: Frau Brunner has been typing since six. The minutes office gets tea from twelve; the buffet is for the delegations.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.l1: Forgive me, Herr Adler. I’ve been typing since six. If the lines start to swim in a moment, it won’t be the ribbon’s fault.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.l2: Doesn’t the minutes office get a break?
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.l3: Tea from twelve. The buffet in the foyer is for the delegations.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.l4: Nobody has touched it yet. Whoever reaches first gives way first – that’s how it’s seen here.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.l5: I’m only a draughtsman. If I give way, nobody will notice.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.ask.l6: Then take something that doesn’t rustle. Cheese doesn’t rustle.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.take.title: First to reach
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.take.text: I put bread and two slices of cheese on a napkin and fold it like a plan, edge to edge. The head of the Soviet delegation watches me do it. Then she takes a slice of bread with caviar, bites into it and looks out of the window. So we have both given way. Over by the photo wall, Nils Ekdahl writes something in his notebook.
Nils Ekdahl saw who reached first. He won’t print it, but he will write it down.
Herr Adler! You opened the buffet. Which delegation was that – yours or the Soviet one?
The minutes office reached first. That’s the best story of this conference.
No. But I’ll write it down – for the book I’ll write in twenty years.
And now take that bread away before the cheese becomes history.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.return.text: Frau Brunner has eaten, between two carbon copies. Today she types my terms with particular care, in all three languages.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.return.l1: Bread and cheese. As promised: it doesn’t rustle.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.return.l2: Folded edge to edge. You can tell the draughtsman.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.return.l3: Fräulein Weiss usually brings me an apple every morning. Not today.
strings.explore.veltrava.task.buffet.return.l6: Thank you, Herr Adler. I’ll type your terms with particular care today. In all three languages.
